restatements.text: Requires a permit issued by the county sheriff to carry a concealed handgun.
Directs the sheriff to issue the permit to applicants who are at least 21 years old, legally permitted to possess a handgun, and have completed an eight-hour safety course.

evidence.quote: No person may carry a concealed handgun without a concealed carry permit
evidence.why: It introduces a new requirement to hold a permit in order to carry a concealed handgun.
It establishes a mandatory eight-hour training requirement to obtain the permit.

evidence.quote: The sheriff shall issue a permit
evidence.why: It assigns a new regulatory mandate and administrative program to county sheriffs.

analysis.answer: Current law allows lawful possessors who are 21 or older to carry a concealed handgun without a permit. The measure changes this by establishing a permit requirement to carry a concealed handgun.

Compared to current law, which has no permit or training requirement for concealed carry, this clause sets criteria for permit issuance: being 21 or older, being legally allowed to possess a handgun, and completing an eight-hour safety course.

Individuals seeking to carry a concealed handgun will bear the direct cost of enrolling in an eight-hour safety course and the opportunity cost of their time. County sheriffs will bear administrative costs for processing applications and issuing permits.

Handgun owners pay the time and financial costs required to complete the training and obtain the permit. Firearms instructors benefit from a new pool of paying customers mandated to take the course. Local law enforcement agencies bear the unstated cost of administering the permitting system.

Some individuals who would have carried a firearm under the permitless system may opt not to due to the cost and time of the mandated class. Firearm safety instructors are likely to increase their offerings to accommodate the new regulatory demand.

The measure addresses the perceived risk of untrained individuals carrying hidden firearms in public. By requiring an eight-hour course, the mechanism aims to ensure a baseline level of safety and competence. Conversely, it creates an entry barrier that limits access to concealed carry for those with lower incomes or less flexible schedules.

Private firearms instructors gain a concentrated benefit through guaranteed demand for their safety courses. County sheriffs gain administrative authority, although their discretion is constrained by the "shall issue" mandate.

Researchers disagree on the effects of moving from permitless carry to permitted carry. Some studies suggest stricter permitting reduces gun homicides and accidental shootings by limiting public carry and ensuring training. Other studies find that widespread permitted carry deters crime and that restricting it disarms law-abiding citizens, leading to higher victimization.

flags.quote: The sheriff shall issue a permit
flags.note: The measure requires county sheriffs to issue permits but does not specify a funding source or authorize application fees to cover administrative costs.
